subject: Renewal + add GPUs: proposed SOW & discount approval needed
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.ai>
To: Marta Silva <marta@acme-corp.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 12 Jan 2026 09:15:00 -0800
Subject: Renewal + proposed dedicated add-on (8 GPUs)

Marta —

Thanks again for the time last week. Per our conversation, Acme's current Dedicated pool renewal is up for renewal on Feb 15. You mentioned you want to expand capacity to support a new realtime feature: adding 8x A100-equivalent GPUs (reserved pool) and a higher throughput SLA for prioritised inference during business hours.

High-level proposal I'm putting on the table:
- Term: 24 months (aligns with your roadmap)
- Additional capacity: 8 GPUs in a dedicated reserved pool (isolated)
- Throughput guarantee: 180 tokens/sec aggregate for the added pool during 8am–8pm PT (SLO + credits for breaches)
- Commercial: mrr increase tied to reserved capacity + one-time onboarding for scaling the cache and prefix warm-up

You asked about discounts/credits if we expand at renewal. Im escalating internally to confirm what we can offer for a mutually beneficial package. Attached is a draft SOW and a capacity addendum with rough pricing (pro_forma_pricing.csv).

Can you confirm the target start date for the new pool (week of Mar 2?) and whether a 24-month term is required, or if 12 months would work for Acme? Ill come back with what we can do on credits.

Best,
Jonas
Account Executive — Redwood Inference
jonas@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0123

Attachments: SOW_Renewal_v2.pdf (draft), capacity_addendum.xlsx (capacity matrix), pro_forma_pricing.csv (pricing mock)
From: Marta Silva <marta@acme-corp.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 13 Jan 2026 10:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Renewal + proposed dedicated add-on (8 GPUs)

Thanks Jonas — this looks like the right direction. A couple quick asks from procurement/engineering:

- Can you provide a one-page cost breakdown that separates reserved GPU commitment from operational fees?
- We'd prefer a 12-month initial term with an option to extend to 24 months after we validate the feature in production.
- On credits: Acme is requesting a one-time onboarding credit to offset the migration/testing effort (theyre asking for an equivalent of ~25% of the first quarter incremental spend). Can you confirm if Redwood can accommodate an onboarding credit at renewal?

If you can send the cost breakdown and a confirmation on credits by Friday, procurement will schedule a follow-up to get legal involved.

— Marta
VP Product Operations, Acme Corp
From: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Dylan Brooks <dylan@redwood.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 14 Jan 2026 08:40:00 -0800
Subject: Fwd: Renewal + proposed dedicated add-on — customer asking for 25% Q1 onboarding credit

Marissa / Dylan —

Looping you both in. Acme wants a one-time onboarding credit roughly equal to 25% of the first quarter incremental spend if we add 8 GPUs at renewal. Theyre also requesting a 12-month term (with option to extend).

My recommendation for a fast close is: offer a limited onboarding credit tied to milestones (not just usage), e.g.:
- Option A (preferred by AE): 15% credit against the first quarter incremental committed spend, applied as a one-time invoice credit after production readiness (warm-up complete).
- Option B (compromise): $90k one-time credit capped, plus a 12-month term with an automatic review at month 9 for extension.

Key commercial considerations:
- We need to protect unit economics if the customer bursts beyond the expected throughput.
- Tying credit to milestones helps reduce risk (e.g., go-live + successful throughput tests).

Can you advise what finance and sales leadership are comfortable approving without executive sign-off? If we need an uplift, I can ask for a formal exception.

Thanks,
Jonas
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 15 Jan 2026 11:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Fwd: Renewal + proposed dedicated add-on — customer asking for 25% Q1 onboarding credit

Jonas —

Thanks for the context. Im supportive of an onboarding concession here to keep Acme on a longer-term commitment, but we should cap the exposure. Finance: please see proposed structure below and confirm whether we can sign off without exec escalation.

Proposed commercial guardrails (sales leadership):
- Approved credit: up to $95,000 one-time onboarding credit, conditional on:
  - Signed SOW amendment for additional 8 GPUs and 12-month committed term, with an option to extend to 24 months at mutually agreed pricing.
  - Production acceptance criteria met (throughput tests within 10% of agreed SLA) within 60 days of pool activation.
  - Credit applied as invoice credit within 30 days after acceptance.
- If Acme extends to 24 months within 90 days, well consider an additional strategic rebate (separate approval).

Please confirm whether finance needs a different cap or any accounting concerns. If finance signs off, Jonas: you can communicate the offer to Acme and ask procurement to confirm.

— Marissa
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 16 Jan 2026 09:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Re: Fwd: Renewal + proposed dedicated add-on — customer asking for 25% Q1 onboarding credit

Marissa / team —

I ran the numbers with accounting. We can approve a one-time credit capped between $90k–$100k, but recommend the following controls for compliance and ASC accounting:

- Final cap: $95,000 one-time credit (to be booked as a contra-revenue adjustment tied to this deal).
- Credit should be milestone-gated: 50% after successful warm-up and KV-cache validation, 50% after SLA acceptance testing.
- Require the amended SOW and a signed DocuSign envelope prior to credit recognition.
- Finance will need the pro-forma and updated revenue schedule before final posting.

Given this fits within Marissa's suggested cap, no C-level escalation required. Jonas: please update the SOW with the 12-month term + extension option and send to Acme with the DocuSign link.

Thanks,
Dylan
Director, Finance Ops — Redwood Inference
From: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.ai>
To: Marta Silva <marta@acme-corp.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Dylan Brooks <dylan@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 20 Jan 2026 14:02:00 -0800
Subject: Final: Renewal SOW & onboarding credit confirmation (DL-2026-0473)

Marta —

Thanks for the quick responses. We reviewed internally and can offer Acme the onboarding concession as follows:

- One-time onboarding credit: $95,000 (applied as invoice credit after milestones).
- Term: 12 months initial, with an option to extend to 24 months at agreed pricing.
- Milestones: 50% of credit after successful warm-up/KV-cache validation; remaining 50% after SLA acceptance testing (within 60 days of activation).
- Updated SOW & capacity addendum attached. Please review the SOW and sign via DocuSign by Jan 31 to lock the pricing and capacity target for the Mar 2 start window. DocuSign link: https://docusign.net/envelope/ABC12345

If that timeline works, Procurement can route to legal and well coordinate kickoff with our Dedicated ops team.

Best,
Jonas
Account Executive — Redwood Inference
